Beginner cycling cadence explained

Cadence is how many times your pedals turn each minute. Most new riders push a heavy gear at a slow cadence, which tires the legs quickly and strains the knees.

Aim for a pace of seventy to ninety revolutions a minute on flat ground. Shift to an easier gear until the pedals feel light and the legs spin without effort.

A cheap cycling computer with a cadence sensor makes this easy to practise. After a few weeks you will find the right gear without looking.
